requirements.sourceText: Foundation Courses (43-46 credits): BIO 201 - Fundamentals of Biology: Organisms to Ecosystems 3 credits; BIO 202 - Fundamentals of Biology: Molecular and Cellular Biology 3 credits; BIO 203 - Fundamentals of Biology: Cellular and Organ Physiology 3 credits; BIO 204 - Fundamentals of Scientific Inquiry in the Biological Sciences I 2 credits; BIO 205 - Fundamentals of Scientific Inquiry in the Biological Sciences IIA 2 credits (see Note 3); CHE 131 - General Chemistry IB 4 credits (see Note 4 and Note 6); CHE 133 - General Chemistry Laboratory I 1 credit (see Note 4 and Note 6); CHE 132 - General Chemistry II 4 credits (see Note 4 and Note 6); CHE 134 - General Chemistry Laboratory II 1 credit (see Note 4 and Note 6); CHE 321 - Organic Chemistry I 4 credits (see Note 5 and Note 6); MAT 125 - Calculus A 3 credits OR MAT 125 - Calculus A Credits: 3 credits MAT 130 - Trigonometry and Logarithms 1 credit, MAT 126 - Calculus B 3 credits; ENS 119 - Physics for Environmental Studies 4 credits PHY 119 - Physics for Environmental Studies 4 credits AND MAR 352 - Introduction to Physical Oceanography 3 credits OR PHY 121 - Physics for the Life Sciences I 4 credits PHY 122 - Physics for the Life Sciences II 4 credits OR PHY 121 - Physics for the Life Sciences I Credits: 4 credits MAR 352 - Introduction to Physical Oceanography Credits: 3 credits; AMS 102 - Elements of Statistics 3 credits; AMS 110 - Probability and Statistics in the Life Sciences 3 credits

requirements.label: zoology-core
requirements.title: Zoology and Marine Vertebrate Core (13 credits)
requirements.sourceText: Zoology and Marine Vertebrate Core (13 credits): MAR 362 - Marine Vertebrate Biology 4 credits OR BIO 344 - Chordate Zoology 4 credits; BIO 354 - Evolution 3 credits OR BIO 320 - General Genetics 3 credits OR BIO 321 - Ecological Genetics 3 credits; Two of the following: MAR 370 - Marine Mammals 3 credits; MAR 373 - Marine Apex Predators: Ecology and Conservation 3 credits; MAR 376 - Biology and Conservation of Sea Turtles 3 credits; MAR 377 - Biology and Conservation of Seabirds 3 credits; MAR 380 - Ichthyology 3 credits

requirements.label: marine-biology
requirements.title: Marine Biology (12-16 credits)
requirements.sourceText: Marine Biology (12-16 credits): MAR 349 - Introduction to Biological Oceanography 4 credits OR MAR 303 - Long Island Marine Habitats 4 credits OR MAR 388 - Tropical Marine Ecology 4 credits; Three electives from below: BIO 328 - Mammalian Physiology 3 credits; BIO 342 - Invertebrate Zoology 3 credits; BIO 351 - Ecology 3 credits; BIO 353 - Marine Ecology 3 credits; EBH 359 - Behavioral Ecology 3 credits; MAR 301 - Environmental Microbiology 4 credits; MAR 302 - Marine Microbiology and Microbial Ecology 3 credits; MAR 303 - Long Island Marine Habitats 4 credits; MAR 305 - Experimental Marine Biology 3 credits; MAR 315 - Marine Conservation 3 credits; MAR 375 - Marine Mammal and Sea Turtle Rehabilitation 3 credits; MAR 384 - Diseases of Aquatic Organisms 3 credits; MAR 385 - Principles of Fishery Biology and Management 3 credits; MAR 386 - Ecosystem Science for Fisheries Management 3 credits; MAR 388 - Tropical Marine Ecology 4 credits; MAR 394 - Environmental Toxicology and Public Health 3 credits; MAR 487 - Research in Marine Sciences 0-6 credits; MAR 488 - Internship 0-6 credits. Notes: These courses can be used as electives if not used as an alternative to MAR 349. Other classes may be substituted with permission of undergraduate director

requirements.sourceText: The advanced writing component of the major in MVB requires registration in, and satisfactory completion of, the 0-credit MAR 459 or SUS 459 (S/U grading) along with enrollment in an approved advanced course that entails writing of either a term paper or a laboratory report. Completion of MAR 459 or SUS 459 with a grade of S will also result in fulfillment of the WRTD requirement. A list of preapproved courses can be found at http://www.somas.stonybrook.edu/education/undergraduate/. Successful completion of BIO 459 will also be accepted for MVB majors.

substitutions.sourceText: MAT 131, MAT 132 or MAT 141, MAT 142 or MAT 171 or AMS 151, AMS 161 may be substituted for MAT 125, MAT 126.
CHE 152 may be substituted for CHE 131 +CHE 132.
CHE 331 may be substituted for CHE 321.
ANT 300 (formerly ANP 300) Human Anatomy or HAN 200 Human Anatomy and Physiology for Health Science I may be substituted for MAR 362 or BIO 344.

notes.text: All students should consult with the director of undergraduate studies to design and approve an acceptable course of study before declaring the major.

Unparsed or unmodeled alternatives in the source: (1) CHE 129/CHE 130 may be substituted for CHE 131. (2) CHE 152, CHE 154 and CHE 331 may be substituted for CHE 131/CHE 132/CHE 133/CHE 134/CHE 321. (3) Several two-semester physics sequences (PHY 125/PHY 126 with PHY 133, PHY 127/PHY 134, PHY 131/PHY 133, PHY 132/PHY 134, PHY 141/PHY 133, PHY 142/PHY 134) may substitute for the physics sequences in the Foundation Courses, and MAR 352 may substitute for PHY 127/PHY 134, PHY 132/PHY 134 or PHY 142/PHY 134. (4) Other classes may be substituted with permission of the undergraduate director.

The Marine Vertebrate Biology Honors Program requires a 3.50 GPA in all courses for the major by the end of the junior year, application to the SoMAS undergraduate director, an honors thesis, and a 3.5 GPA through senior year with a recommendation from the undergraduate research committee. This optional program is not modeled.
The BS/MS program in Marine Vertebrate Biology is temporarily suspended effective Spring 2026. Accelerated programs are not modeled.
